strongest_angle: Examine the court docket where New York Supreme Court Justice Leslie A. Stroth temporarily stayed proceedings in the $275,000 Jingle Ball lawsuit involving Nicki Minaj and Pink Friday Productions LLC after attorney Bruce W. Bieber stated the attorney-client relationship had irretrievably broken down.

key_facts.fact: New York Supreme Court Justice Leslie A. Stroth signed an October 27, 2026 order staying all proceedings in a $275,000 lawsuit involving Nicki Minaj and Pink Friday Productions LLC.

Attorney Bruce W. Bieber of Kurzman Eisenberg Corbin & Lever LLP stated in court papers filed on October 23, 2026, that the attorney-client relationship with Nicki Minaj has irretrievably broken down.
A New York judge paused the $275,000 Jingle Ball dispute and set a December hearing regarding the legal team's request to withdraw from representing Nicki Minaj.
The $275,000 lawsuit against Nicki Minaj and Pink Friday Productions LLC was filed by 24/7 Productions over her 2023 Jingle Ball run.

quotes.text: the attorney-client relationship has irretrievably broken down such that continued representation is no longer feasible or appropri
